versions.name: RXV2-0.9.444-imu-first
versions.notes: First-time basics reordered per Malcolm: 'Calibrate the flight controller' (IMU) is now the FIRST card - best done flat on a desk before the board goes in (the helicopter may not sit level), and front-or-back mounting does not affect it (the old 'set mounting first' note was wrong for flat boards). Wizard step 4 renamed to match.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.443-model-memory
versions.notes: Wizard step 3: 'Create a new model memory on your transmitter' - the proper term.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.442-fw-recommended
versions.notes: Wizard step 1 is now 'Firmware update (recommended)' - update via the computer Configurator before you begin (new boards do fly as delivered).

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.441-default-port
versions.notes: Wiring page: the port rule stated plainly - plug into the default receiver port (ELRS/RX) and it just works; any other port needs one configurator visit first.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.440-rx-port
versions.notes: Wiring page: which UART, answered - use the port labelled for the receiver (ELRS/RX), pre-configured for CRSF out of the box, nothing to declare. Any other UART is a chicken-and-egg that needs one configurator visit on USB.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.439-wiring-page
versions.notes: New Wiring page inside the New-helicopter wizard (Malcolm's spec): every plug on one line - S1 = the front-or-back servo then clockwise round the swash, tail on S4, ESC throttle lead, the one-wire telemetry to TLM, the RPM wire if your ESC has one, and the receiver's UART (CRSF). Head speed must arrive by telemetry or RPM wire, or the governor has nothing to govern.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.438-visible-text
versions.notes: Readability pass (Malcolm's suggestions): the Back button is now bright green - findable at a glance instead of blending into the meadow; and every loose line of text sits on its own solid panel, no more faint words straight on the background photo.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.437-lean-wizard
versions.notes: The wizards on a diet (Malcolm: easier to follow, dyslexia-friendly): every checklist step and intro is now one short action-first line - New helicopter, Tuning, First-time basics, Transmitter channels. All the detail still lives behind each page's ? button.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.436-rf-never-forgotten
versions.notes: Three field reports from Malcolm's test day: (1) the Rotorflight options can no longer be forgotten - once Rotorflight is seen it STAYS seen (latched in the receiver for the whole boot, and remembered per model in the app) so detection flickers never hide the button; (2) the app's demo now carries full servo/rescue/switches/first-time data (no more 'undefined servos'); (3) the wave-test message explains that on a Rotorflight heli a rudder wave is invisible (yaw is a rate command the FC ignores while disarmed) - use ch1 aileron.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.435-pulse-spool
versions.notes: Malcolm's 'manual PWM' idea for neXt spool-up, built: PULSE MODE on the spool-up card - while spooling, the motor channel blips between full off and full on with a rising on-share (period adjustable, try 250 ms), so the sim's own rotor inertia averages it into a genuine head-speed climb even though neXt treats the motor as a pure switch. Two-speed bailout, torque stab and all existing behaviour unchanged; pulse off = exactly the old ramp.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.434-nudge-manners
versions.notes: The back-up-your-tune reminder now has manners: completing a backup (from either the Backup page or Black box) signs off the current tune generation, so the banner goes away and STAYS away until a setting actually changes - then it returns after six unchanged flights, exactly as before.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.433-clocked-events
versions.notes: Two from Malcolm's bench log: (1) BUG FIX - with an arming channel known, the old 'link live 30s = flying' rule fought the new disarm revival, flapping the radios every 5 seconds on the bench with the transmitter on; ARMED is now the only definition of flying on such models (the old rule remains for models without arming). (2) The event log now shows the TIME OF DAY for every event once a phone has taught the receiver the clock - retroactively for events logged before the sync; time-since-boot before that.
